I have been farming in Iringa for many years, and this 0.93-hectare plot is where I grow maize with beans intercropped. The soil here is good, so I will apply some DAP and urea—about what I can afford in one season—to help the maize grow well, and I also have manure from my cattle to mix in. I will plant improved seed because it gives me better harvests than the local variety, but I do not use chemicals for pests or irrigation since the rains are usually enough. My family will do most of the work, but I will hire a few young men to help with weeding when the crops are tall.
